data.name: CodeGen_Error_MultiTargetEfCoreExclusive
data.value: EF Core generation cannot be combined with multi-target QuickER Repositories (two or more effective dialects). Narrow it to a single dialect or disable EF Core (the two are mutually exclusive).

data.value: Column '{1}' of table '{0}' resolves to different C# types across dialects ({2}: {3} / {4}: {5}). The shared Entity is a single type, so both dialects must resolve to the same C# type.

data.name: CodeGen_Error_RepositoryRequiresDataAnnotations
data.value: Repository / EF Core / in-memory Repository use the [Table] / [Key] / [Column] attributes, so data annotations must be applied. Enable data annotations.

data.name: CodeGen_Error_RemoteRequiresContract
data.value: Remote support (GenerateRemoteContracts / GenerateRemoteServices) extends the repository contract, so no remote code is produced without one. Enable GenerateRepositories, GenerateEfCore, or GenerateInMemoryRepositories, or turn the remote options off.

data.name: CodeGen_Error_EntityClassNameCollision
data.value: Tables {1} all map to the same entity class name '{0}'. Entity classes are partial, so they would merge into a single class and fail to compile. Rename the tables so that the generated class names differ (table names are singularized, so 'customer' and 'customers' both become 'CustomerEntity').

data.name: CodeGen_Error_ColumnPropertyNameCollision
data.value: Columns {2} of table '{0}' all map to the same property name '{1}'. The entity and EditModel classes would declare duplicate members and fail to compile. Rename the columns so that the generated property names differ (column names are converted to Pascal case, so 'user-id', 'user_id', and 'USER_ID' all become 'UserId').

data.name: CodeGen_Error_MultipleRowVersionColumns
data.value: Table '{0}' has more than one rowversion column ({1}). Optimistic concurrency reads and writes a single version column per table, and SQL Server allows only one as well, so the DDL would fail on the second one. Keep one rowversion column and give the others another type.

data.name: CodeGen_Error_PrimaryKeyRowVersionColumn
data.value: Column '{1}' of table '{0}' is both the primary key and a rowversion column. A rowversion is assigned by the database, so it is left out of every INSERT and UPDATE the repositories issue: the generated INSERT would send no key at all, and the row's identity would rest on a value that changes with every update. Give the primary key a type of its own, and add a separate rowversion column if the table needs optimistic concurrency.

data.name: CodeGen_Error_PrimaryKeyUnboundedBinaryColumn
data.value: Column '{1}' of table '{0}' is both the primary key and an unbounded binary column, and unbounded binary columns are excluded (ExcludeUnboundedBinaryColumns). An excluded column is left out of every SELECT the repositories issue, so the key would not be read back: GetByIdAsync and GetAllAsync would return entities whose key is null, and any save built on them would target the wrong row. Give the primary key a bounded type of its own, or turn the exclusion off.

data.name: CodeGen_Error_GeneratedMemberNameCollision
data.value: Class '{0}' (table '{1}') generates the member name '{2}' more than once (from {3}). The same member would be declared twice and fail to compile (CS0102). Rename the columns so that every generated member name is unique. Note that an EditModel generates five members per column (Name, _name, BindingName, _bindingName, _bindingNameSnapshot), so a column named 'binding_id' collides with the members generated for a column named 'id', and a column whose property name equals a navigation property name (for example a column named 'customer' on a table that references the 'customers' table) collides on the entity class as well.
